text: A real time auction platform. Sellers list items with a starting price and an end time, bidders place bids and everyone watching an item sees new bids live without reloading. When time runs out the highest bidder wins. Bidders want to see prices in their own currency, so use a public exchange rate API. It should run as several services (an API server and a separate live update server) so it can scale.

I saved the first draft with 7 requirements.

- **Functional (REQ-001 to REQ-005):** sellers list items with a starting price and end time. Bidders place bids. Watchers see new bids live without reloading. The auction closes at the end time and the highest bidder wins. Prices show in the bidder's currency, using a public exchange rate API.
- **Non-functional (REQ-006, REQ-007):** the system runs as separate services, with an API server and a live update server. Each can be scaled independently by running more instances.

I recorded no assumptions and nothing as out of scope yet. My questions are below.

1. Do users need accounts and login, and what roles exist (seller, bidder, admin)? Can a seller bid on their own item?
2. What are the bid rules? Must a bid exceed the current highest bid, is there a minimum increment, and should a late bid extend the end time?
3. In which currency are starting prices and bids entered and stored: the seller's, one fixed base currency, or the bidder's? Is the conversion for display only?
4. What should happen if the exchange rate API is unavailable? Do you have a preferred API, and is there a limit on how old a cached rate may be?
5. What are the scale and latency targets (concurrent watchers, bids per second, maximum delay for a live update)? Also, what happens when an auction ends with no bids, and are payment and winner notification in scope?

1. No passwords: users pick a display name, stored in the browser; the server keeps a user id per name. Roles are just seller and bidder, any user can be both. No admin. A seller cannot bid on their own item. 2. A bid must exceed the current highest bid (or be at least the starting price for the first bid) by at least 1 unit of the item currency. A bid in the last 2 minutes extends the end time by 2 minutes. 3. The seller picks the item currency (CHF, EUR or USD); bids are entered and stored in that currency. Conversion is display only. 4. Use Frankfurter (api.frankfurter.app, no key). Cache rates for 1 hour; if the API is down, show only the item currency. 5. Demo scale: up to 200 watchers per item, a few bids per second, live updates within 1 second. No bids means the item ends unsold. Payment and notifications are out of scope; the winner just sees they won on the item page.

I saved the updated document. It now has 11 requirements, and I removed the five questions you answered.

- **Changed:**
  - REQ-001: the seller also picks the item currency (CHF, EUR or USD).
  - REQ-002: a seller can't bid on their own item. A first bid must be at least the starting price. Later bids must beat the highest bid by at least 1 unit. Bids are stored in the item currency.
  - REQ-004: an auction with no bids ends as unsold. The winner sees on the item page that they won.
  - REQ-005: conversion uses Frankfurter and is for display only.
- **Added:**
  - REQ-008: display-name identity with no password, a name stored in the browser, one server-side user id per name, and no admin.
  - REQ-009: a valid bid in the last 2 minutes extends the end time by 2 minutes.
  - REQ-010: rates are cached for 1 hour. If the API is down and no valid cached rate exists, prices show only in the item currency.
  - REQ-011: up to 200 watchers per item, a few bids per second, and live updates within 1 second.
- **Out of scope:** payment, notifications, passwords and login, and scale beyond the demo level.

Two questions remain:

1. **Q-006:** Can users pick any display name? If a name is already taken, should the system reject it, or let the new browser reuse that user id?
2. **Q-007:** Which currencies can a bidder choose for display: only CHF, EUR and USD, or any currency Frankfurter supports?
Q-006: names are unique, 2 to 20 characters; a taken name is rejected and the user must pick another. The browser keeps the user id it got. Q-007: only CHF, EUR and USD.

I saved the updated document. It still has 11 requirements, and no questions are open.

- **REQ-008:** display names must be unique and 2 to 20 characters long. A taken name is rejected and the user must pick another. The server keeps one user id per name, and the browser stores the id it received.
- **REQ-005:** bidders can choose only CHF, EUR or USD as their display currency.
- **Out of scope:** I added display currencies other than CHF, EUR and USD.

I removed Q-006 and Q-007, and there are no assumptions. Let me know if you want any changes. Otherwise you can approve this for the next phase.
